Never repeat the masthead's destinations in the mat. Footer's own meta says it: a doormat that duplicates the masthead is a doormat that has stopped being read.
Never make a sticky header without giving anchor targets a scroll-margin. The jump will land the reader behind the band and nothing will look wrong until someone tries it.
Never let the sticky offset and the scroll-margin be two separate numbers. They will drift the first time somebody changes the band's height.
Never put a mega-footer on an authenticated task screen. That is App-shell-focused's territory, and a list of ways to leave is not what a person mid-payment needs.
Never give the mat a breakpoint. auto-fit/minmax already re-flows it, and a duplicated rule is a rule that will one day contradict the behaviour it duplicates.
Never let a back-to-top control move the view without moving the focus.
Never put the primary navigation back in. The moment a focused shell offers five destinations it has become App-shell-top-nav and the user has five new ways to abandon the task.
Never make the exit a bare glyph on a multi-step task. A ✕ with no name discards work silently, and the user cannot tell whether it saves.
Never carry two progress statements on one screen. Pick the shell's band or the template's step rail — see $finding-progress-collision.
Never put a doormat footer here. A mega-footer at the end of a sign-in form is a list of ways to leave.
Never keep a bordered card at phone width. It costs reading width and separates the form from nothing.
Never use form=task for a single-screen job. A progress bar reading 'step 1 of 1' is an insult to the reader.
Never hide the inactive pane with visibility or a transform. It must leave the tab order and the accessibility tree, or a keyboard user will end up inside a pane that is not on screen.
Never return focus to the top of the list when the user comes back from a record. They lose their place every single time.
Never mark the current row with colour alone. It is a shape first and a hue third.
Never let the detail pane keep the previous record's title while the new one loads. Retitle first, then load — otherwise the heading is lying about what is underneath it.
Never grow the rail to a full column in this frame. Three panes is already the widest this can be, and the room would come out of the list.
Never invent a filter bar in the list header. Row 120 owns that artefact.
Never paint status colour into the frame. A shell has nothing to be red about.
Never give a label flyout an accessible name. The link already has one, and announcing it twice is a stutter no gate will catch.
Never leave a menu flyout aria-hidden. It carries destinations; hiding it removes them from the only users who cannot see the icons.
Never open a menu flyout on hover. It opens by accident and it closes mid-reach.

Never make a hover-revealed panel pointer-events:none. It is not a target, the pointer passes through it, and it disappears exactly when the user reaches for it — SC 1.4.13's hoverable clause, failed.
Never build a hover flyout without a dismiss route. A :hover rule cannot be dismissed and SC 1.4.13 requires that it can.
Never add an expand toggle. That component exists and it is App-shell-side-nav.
Never put more than five destinations in the phone bar, and never put a long name in one. Four short names fit; five long ones truncate to nonsense.
Never make the query container the flex parent. The main axis belongs to the parent and a container query may not touch it.
Never let the drawer carry a different set of destinations from the column it replaced.
Never remove a label to make a rail — hide it. A removed label takes the accessible name with it and the link becomes an anonymous glyph.
Never let the container query silently overrule a user who has just pressed the toggle. Inside the band where both states are legal, the person wins.
Never omit the skip link. This is the pattern where the bypass block matters most: without it every page starts with the app bar and the whole nav column.
Never mark the current location with colour alone. The bar is a shape first and a hue third.
Never paint status colour into the frame. A shell has nothing to be red about.
Never use a split where one pane drives the other. That is App-shell-multi-column, and it has a rail, a list and a detail for a reason.
Never give the two panes different chrome. The moment one has a toolbar the other lacks, the user reads it as the important one and the component has become something else.
Never make the fences asymmetric. An asymmetric fence is a ranking expressed in pixels.
Never publish the divider's position in pixels. Pixels do not survive a resize, an axis change, a hidden tab panel or a print stylesheet — the percentage is the thing the user chose.
Never keep a drag-to-resize separator at phone width. It cannot be operated by touch with any precision and it offers arrow keys to a device that has none.
Never put a third pane in. A split is two.
Never stack the nav onto a second band just because there is room. A band of chrome is vertical space the content never gets back, and on a laptop that is the fold.
Never let the section tier wrap to two rows. It scrolls horizontally instead — two rows of section nav is a nav that has outgrown the pattern.
Never replace the breadcrumb trail with an ellipsis at phone width. Keep the last ancestor: the trail exists to get back, and getting back is what a phone user does most.
Never let the off-canvas sheet carry a different set of destinations from the row it replaced. A nav that changes contents when it changes shape is teaching two maps of one building.
